Rafael,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 502s at ~09:05 PT and 95th percentile latency jumped from ~480ms to ~2.1s for our inference calls. Throughput has dropped ~60% (successful QPS down from 420 -> ~170) and clients are timing out. Error rate is currently 18% on our production model route (model: gptf-2-large).

We need immediate containment. Can Redwood steer traffic off US-WEST-2 to another region? Our SLA team is getting blasted and the health dashboard is red across multiple services. We can accept some short tail latency increase during a regional failover if it stabilizes. Please advise immediate next steps and ETA.

Attachments: sentinel_5xx_logs_0612.zip (logs from 08:55–09:10 PT)

-Maya

Maya — thanks for the signal and the logs. I'm escalating this to contain immediately. TL;DR: we will activate the regional containment runbook and propose a staged traffic steer to us-east-2. Need your go/no-go to steer 10% -> 50% -> 100% over the next 20 minutes.

Actions I'm initiating now (will update in-thread):
- Activating Incident Runbook: "regional-evacuation-v2" (I will attach the steering playbook).
- Ask network and serving teams to check AZ health in US-WEST-2 (logging team already pulling kernel/host-level metrics).
- Prep cross-region routing: canary steer to us-east-2; fallback policy will be automatic to previous region if error rate increases >5% from baseline after steer.

Risk notes: a full steer will increase median latency for some routed sessions due to cross-region RTT, and may consume additional capacity in us-east-2. We can do partial steer first to validate.

Maya, please reply with explicit approval to start the staged steer. Neha / Steph / Vanessa — looping you in for approvals and exec communication. I'll call for a 15-min exec bridge in 30 minutes unless you advise otherwise.

Attaching: steer-playbook-v3.pdf, runbook-redeploy-steps.pdf

-Rafael

Team — runbook activated and ops playbook running. Summary of immediate steps completed:
1) Confirmed spike source appears related to AZ host-network flapping in us-west-2 (control-plane events correlate with logs).
2) Warmed additional serving pools in us-east-2 (quantized + float variants) to accept overflow.
3) Initialized staged steer plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 20m windows with health checks at 2m intervals.
4) KV-cache prefix replication started for stateful sessions to reduce cold-start overhead.

Requesting approval: Rafael / Neha: please approve staged steer now. If approved, we'll start the 10% shift immediately and monitor 95th/99th latencies and 502 rate.

Estimated containment timeline if approved: 10–25 minutes to see initial stabilization; full normalization 60–90 minutes depending on cache warm-up and capacity.

Attachment: steer-playbook-v3.pdf (contains rollback criteria)
